sources.spatial: 1 km grid, the inner Danish waters subset
sources.aggregation: per-measurement per cell per day. It is a SATELLITE RETRIEVAL, not a cell count: functional-type chlorophyll is derived from total chl by the Brando et al. (2021) abundance-based algorithm.
sources.coverage: 1997-2025 as downloaded; the product itself runs to near-present
sources.size: ~711 MB per full year, 29 yearly files
sources.caveat: THIS CHANGES K1 AND IT IS ALREADY DOWNLOADED. The last pass concluded that K1's diatom-share term needed an authenticated ICES DOME extraction because OBIS and GBIF strip the cell counts. It does not: a DIATOM CHLOROPHYLL FIELD, daily, at 1 km, for twenty years, is sitting in data/raw/cmems/grid, and the Si:N ratio to regress it against is in ODA at the same dates. K1's discriminator - the Si:N ratio through time against the diatom share of the community - can be computed this week. Three real limits, all of which must be carried: (1) it is a RETRIEVAL, and the file's own metadata states a chlorophyll validity range of 0.13-25.5 mg m-3, so blooms above that are clipped; (2) the Danish straits are optically complex Case-2 water where ocean-colour chlorophyll is least reliable and where CDOM and resuspended sediment interfere - which is Z8's argument applied to the satellite rather than to the field measurement; (3) diatom chlorophyll is inferred from total chlorophyll by an abundance-based model, so a diatom share derived from it is not independent of total biomass in the way a cell count would be. Validate it against the ICES DOME occurrence record before trusting a trend.

sources.caveat: FIFTY-THREE MILLION ROWS OF DANISH MARINE PROFILE DATA BACK TO 1970, ON DISK, AND IT CARRIES FIVE PARAMETERS THE CRITERION PANE DID NOT ADVERTISE. The previous pass read twelve parameters off the portal's criterion list. The data holds seventeen, and the five extra ones matter: FDOM at 890,921 rows, Turbiditet at 1,076,915, Stroemhastighed and Stroemretning at about 84,000 each, Farvestof at 4,601, and Dihydrogensulfid at 2,601. FDOM is fluorescent dissolved organic matter - an in-situ optical proxy for the coloured dissolved organic matter that Z2's browning argument and Z8's attenuation partition are both about - and it has never been used here. Beyond that, this file is what makes Z4 and W6 answerable without any new source: both need high-frequency records analysed for extremes and RATES rather than means, and the records are local. It also carries the raw result beside the corrected one, the correction factor applied, the sonde number and the QA level, so the measurement chain is auditable, which is what group I asks for. TWO PARSING WARNINGS. The encoding is iso-8859-1 and the delimiter is a semicolon, and at least one free-text field contains embedded semicolons - a naive awk -F';' pass put coordinate-like strings into the date column and produced a nonsense date range - so read it as quoted CSV with the right codec. And use KorrigeretResultat rather than OriginalResultat, carrying QANiveau through: 42.5M rows are at 'C, Faglig kontrol', 8.5M at 'D, FDC faglig kontrol' and 2.7M only at 'B, Elektronisk kontrol'.

sources.caveat: A REAL FIND AND A REAL LIMIT, AND THE LIMIT IS THE MORE IMPORTANT OF THE TWO. FDOM - fluorescent dissolved organic matter, the in-situ optical proxy for the coloured dissolved organic matter that Z2's browning argument and Z8's attenuation partition are both about - IS measured in Danish waters, at 211 stations, 890,921 rows, and nobody has used it. But it starts in 2021. Z2's actual claim is that CDOM export has been RISING across Nordic waters, and a five-year sensor record cannot test a trend; what it can do is partition the attenuation budget from 2021 onward, alongside Turbiditet for the particle term and Lysdaempning for the total. That is Z8's discriminator, approximately, for the present rather than for the past. TURBIDITY HAS A THIRTEEN-YEAR HOLE. 1994-2007 sparse, then NOTHING from 2008 to 2020, then dense from 2021. Any turbidity trend computed across that gap is an artefact of instrumentation, not a change in the water, and the same 2021 discontinuity appears in FDOM - both look like one sonde upgrade rolled out across the network. The other two are too small to build on: hydrogen sulphide on the CTD is 4 stations over 2001-2010, and Farvestof is 8 stations over 2001-2005. Neither supports R5 or E12 on its own; the water-chemistry Svovlbrinte parameter remains the sulphide source.

sources.parameters_note: wanted: a UV or photoinhibition ceiling for Danish species (Z1); marine invertebrate phenology keyed to daylength (Z3); a pre-computed marine heatwave index for Danish waters (Z4); measured near-bed currents to validate modelled bed shear (Z5); epiphyte BIOMASS per unit leaf area with grazer abundance (Z9); eelgrass rhizome carbohydrate reserves (Z11)
sources.caveat: SIX WINDOWS, AND THE CEILING IS MISSING FROM EVERY ONE. The pattern is consistent and it is the group's own point: Denmark measures how much of a field there is and never where the upper bound lies. Z1 has an excellent floor - Kd, Lysprocent and Secchi - and no photoinhibition threshold for any Danish species. Z4 has fifty years of temperature and no heatwave index; the Hobday method on the Copernicus reanalysis already on disk would produce one. Z5 has modelled bed shear from 31 years of wind and no measured near-bed current to validate it against. Z9 has epiphyte COVER in ODA and no biomass per leaf area and no grazer count, which are the two quantities its discriminator names. Z11 has no carbohydrate reserve measurement, and the nearest analogues are German (Kiel Bay, sediment burial) and Canadian (St Lawrence, which measures sugar, starch AND epiphyte load together and is the methodological template). Z3 is the only one where no candidate source could even be identified to test.
sources.verified: UNVERIFIED as data - 2026-09-08, sub-agent: each PANGAEA search returned 200 with the top hits inspected and rejected on location; the two failing endpoints recorded with their status

A10.note: The mass term has a proxy and the measurement has none. Danmarks Statistik publishes annual national kilograms under the CN8 code for aqueous urea, 1988-2025, which is the only AdBlue volume figure available - and the code also carries agricultural urea solution, and the series rises from 2009 and falls in 2022-23 rather than stepping at the 2013-15 mandate, so it cannot carry the stepped wedge alone. Fleet composition by Euro class is in no Danmarks Statistik table. The measurement A10 actually rests on - roadside and network ammonia, reduced against oxidised - was not reached: DCE's air-monitoring pages 404 or 500, EBAS holds the Danish EMEP stations behind a legacy interactive interface, and the CLRTAP national NH3-from-road-transport series sits behind a multi-step CGI form. Two of those three are known to exist and need a browser rather than a fetch. EMEP does already give reduced and oxidised deposition separately on a 0.1 degree monthly grid, which is the discriminator's spatial half.

E13.note: Both halves absent, and the second one twice over. Azole, strobilurin and SDHI analyte codes exist nationally - tebuconazole, azoxystrobin, propiconazole, boscalid, epoxiconazole, pyraclostrobin - but only for groundwater and drinking water; ODA's marine sediment topic carries no pesticide at all; and the national river-basin-specific-pollutant network is 256 stations of which zero are coastal and only five measure sediment. The fungal biomass half is worse: no ergosterol, chitin or PLFA measurement anywhere, and ENA holds 1,483 Danish fungal-taxon runs of which not one carries a marine biome tag.

E14.note: VetStat is the right source and DANMAP is not - DANMAP's own page confirms it covers antimicrobials only, so the obvious first guess is wrong. VetStat covers all veterinary products including antiparasitics, its public resolution is by substance group, species, production type, region and quarter, and the per-herd records that would let a catchment load be built are access-controlled. It is also an Angular app that returns nothing readable to a fetch. Ivermectin has a Jupiter groundwater analyte code, so the compound is at least definable in Danish reporting; no manure, soil or sediment residue measurement was found.

E15.note: E15 asks for a summed biocide load per catchment and this pass could not even establish where Danish pesticide SALES data now lives - Miljoestyrelsen's site was reorganised and neither its sitemap nor its successor agency's carries the Bekaempelsesmiddelstatistik. The mandatory spray journals, which would give field resolution, were not chased at all. What does exist is VAP, which measures actual leaching at five or six experimental plots - a different and much narrower question. Treat this as unresolved rather than absent: the annual publication almost certainly still exists at a moved URL.

E16.note: No marine concentration of any azole, strobilurin, SDHI, neonicotinoid or pyrethroid was found, and the structural reason is now quantified: the national status network for river-basin-specific pollutants has 256 stations and none of them is coastal. The legal half is unverified rather than answered - EUR-Lex returned an empty body for the priority-substance directive and retsinformation.dk serves a JavaScript shell, so which of these compound classes is actually regulated in Danish marine water could not be read. E16's own point survives the failure: the endpoint would have to be matched to the conserved target, and Danish testing measures mortality.

E17.note: Three Danish eelgrass host-microbiome datasets exist, none of them with a biocide-exposure axis and none with a host condition variable. E17's claim is that a host can be killed through its symbionts and no toxicity test on the host would see it; testing that needs symbiont composition in exposed against unexposed hosts, and neither the exposure nor the outcome is recorded anywhere Danish.

E18.note: A striking and narrow positive: 6PPD-quinone has a national analyte code in the GEUS Jupiter substance catalogue, stofnr 2730, flagged for both groundwater and drinking water in ug/l - and the number is very high in the sequence, so it is a recent addition. The lead confirmed this directly on the page. What it does NOT prove is that any Danish sample has been analysed: a code makes a parameter reportable, and a sub-agent's inference that unit-conversion factors imply real measurement does not hold, because those tooltips appear on unrelated substances too. The per-borehole sample count for 6PPD-quinone is the obvious next query and would settle it in one call. The marine and road-runoff side remains the confirmed blank the previous pass recorded.

E19.note: No panel of locally present Danish species exists for ecotoxicological testing. This is recorded as a lead rather than a verified fact: the sub-agent could not open DHI's ecotoxicology page and its conclusion that Danish commercial testing uses the standard OECD battery is background knowledge. E19's structure is nonetheless confirmed by E18's own history - 6PPD-quinone passed standard screening for decades.

E20.note: THE STANDOUT POSITIVE OF THIS PASS. Jupiter, the national borehole and groundwater database, carries MTBE, benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, xylenes and BTEX as coded per-borehole analytes across roughly 350,000 boreholes, open, with a bulk export and SOAP services, from the early 1990s. ETBE is absent - the lead searched and found zero hits - so the ether half is half covered. Two limits: an analyte code proves reportability, not that samples exist, and the per-borehole counts were not retrieved; and the entire database is framed around drinking-water abstraction, so E20's coastal-discharge link needs borehole positions overlaid on coastline proximity and a discharge model, which is where the two submarine-groundwater-discharge case studies already on record become relevant.

F11.note: F11 says viral counts are standard since the 1990s and absent from Danish monitoring at every station, and that is right. The one exception is peculiar and worth keeping: real flow-cytometric counts on real Kattegat water, about 3.5 million particles per millilitre, measured inside a hydrostatic-pressure experiment simulating a hadal trench, so the numbers are decoupled from any field position or date. The standing stock of the most abundant biological entity in Danish seawater has been counted once, in a pressure chamber.

F12.note: F12 says Denmark has no mortality-event response capability for invertebrates, and that is too strong. DTU Aqua is the designated National Reference Laboratory for mollusc diseases and runs the national preparedness scheme for aquatic animal disease, with legal backing - a real institutional capability. What could not be established is its resolution: which sites, how often, which species, and whether Bonamia or Marteilia have ever been found here, because the EU decision listing disease-free zones served an empty body. So a listed disease in a commercial mollusc would be caught; whether anything responds to an unexplained die-off of a non-commercial invertebrate remains exactly the open question.

F13.note: ANSWERED, AND THE DATA HAS EXISTED SINCE 2018. F13 says a survey organised as bundfauna, vegetation and phytoplankton has no column for a labyrinthulid or an oomycete, and that metabarcoding is the remedy. Denmark has two ARMS-MBON sites, Limfjorden and Laesoe, with 18S, COI and ITS sequencing across two deployment rounds and about 8,000 occurrence rows published openly through GBIF at per-replicate resolution - entirely outside NOVANA. Add a 2020 Gothenburg-led pilot that sampled nine Danish boulder reefs with 12S, 18S and COI and found 400 species against the diver survey's 184, with 12 per cent overlap. Because 18S is not filtered to a folk category it should catch the between-the-categories organisms; whether labyrinthulid and thraustochytrid OTUs actually appear in the Danish rows was not checked and is a cheap, decisive follow-up.

F14.note: Nothing at all. No Danish marine virome exists in ENA or MGnify - every Danish run with a viral library source is SARS-CoV-2 clinical surveillance, and a virome title search across the whole archive returns 51 studies of which none is Danish. Filtering all 250 Tara Oceans prokaryote-fraction runs by coordinate returns no station inside Danish waters, because the 2009-2013 route did not come here. So the functional layer F14 argues is filed under 'pathogen' and never examined has, in Denmark, not even been counted.

R11.note: Answered in principle and barely in practice. The entire marine fungal barcode record for Denmark is ten ARMS-MBON ITS occurrence rows from one deployment at one Laesoe site, and the parallel round returns zero. Against that, ENA is structurally empty: all 69 Danish ITS runs are a digester, two food metagenomes and a cropland soil, and none of the 1,483 Danish fungal-taxon runs carries a marine biome tag. R11's discriminator needs fungal BIOMASS against the recalcitrant organic fraction, and no biomass measurement of any kind - ergosterol, chitin, PLFA - exists here.

T9.note: The host data exists and the outcome variable does not. Three Danish Zostera marina microbiome datasets - 439 sequencing runs across a rhizosphere-versus-bulk-sediment design, a leaf-associated seasonal series and a 52-day decomposition time series - and not one carries a disease score, a condition index or a survival measure. T9 asks for host condition against symbiont composition under a stress gradient, and the season-and-site axis in these datasets is a proxy for stress rather than a measurement of it.

T10.note: T10's point is that the comparison is made impossible afterwards by construction, and that is what was found. No pre-intervention community baseline was located for any Danish marine intervention. The one intervention dataset with molecular monitoring - an oyster-restoration clay-substrate biofilm succession - starts from bare substrate with no ambient reef community sampled alongside, so it illustrates the problem rather than solving it. The Horsens eelgrass transplant does have a bare-bottom control, which is the closest thing in the register to a baseline, and it is fauna rather than community function.

T11.note: T11 says occupancy is a function with no product and is visible only in what happens when it is removed. Denmark has the first half: an explicit rhizosphere-versus-bulk-sediment design at a north Zealand site, tagged in ENVO terms, and an oyster-restoration biofilm succession framed by its own authors as mediating larval settlement. What is missing is the challenge experiment - invasion or infection success in an intact community against a depleted one - which is the same standard assay as T5's sediment inoculation and has not been run in Danish marine work.

T12.note: No Danish dataset measures a defence phenotype against microbiome composition. T12's sharp end is that a broad-spectrum biocide disarms the host by removing its garrison, and testing that needs the biocide exposure, the symbiont community and the disease outcome together; Denmark has the middle term at three sites and neither of the others anywhere.

W1.note: The source populations are not mapped and the connectivity model is not deposited. EMODnet's pan-European seagrass polygon layer returns ZERO features for the core Danish box, and a wider box returns 36 of which every one is German; the biogenic-substrate layer returns three Danish polygons, one an Ostrea edulis bed and none Mytilus. So there is no national Danish eelgrass or mussel bed layer reachable, and ODA's transect points remain the finest eelgrass resolution - though two Danish GIS hosts failed DNS and Danmarks Arealinformation serves only a JavaScript shell, so a national layer may exist behind a browser. On the model side, a 2024 Skagerrak study combines larval particle-tracking with population genomics for blue mussels, but has one Danish locality out of twenty-five and its connectivity matrix is not deposited. It would have to be rebuilt - and the forcing for that is the 17 GB of CMEMS already on disk.

W2.note: No settlement measurement of any kind in Denmark - three literature searches return nothing, and ODA has no settlement or spat parameter. This is the gap that also disables the biological half of Z6: Denmark now has twelve years of soundscape at eight stations and no settlement rate to test it against.

W3.note: W3 SAYS THE SAMPLING FREQUENCY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND IT IS NOT, AT TWELVE TO FIFTEEN PLACES. The NOVANA programme description states phytoplankton and primary production are sampled 20 times a year at 15 stations, and meso- and microzooplankton 20 times a year at 8 inner-water stations - roughly fortnightly through the growing season, which resolves a bloom peak against larval abundance. Two qualifications: the visits are concentrated seasonally and the calendar spacing must be read off the data, and everything outside those stations gets one visit a year or one every three. The satellite functional-type field on disk gives a daily bloom-timing series to cross-check against. Note also that the DCE technical instructions do not state frequency at all - only the programme description does.

W4.note: The stock-level series exists and is the wrong resolution. ICES publishes annual recruitment and spawning stock biomass for Western Baltic cod 1985-2023 through an open API, but both are model outputs integrated across the whole management area, so the density variation an Allee effect lives in has been averaged away. W4's own text says the fauna data has densities and the analysis is not run, and that is exactly right: ODA carries counts per 143 cm2 grab with 7-10 replicates per visit, which is a real density, at 3,468 historical stations. No ICES-assessed stock exists for Danish blue mussels.

W5.note: W5 calls sub-annual trawling effort the single most important closed dataset and this pass confirms it without opening it. No monthly or quarterly WGSFD swept-area product exists on any reachable ICES page; EMODnet vessel density is monthly but is AIS traffic rather than gear-in-water and misses the small coastal fleet below the carriage threshold; Global Fishing Watch hard-401s every endpoint without a free token, so its documented daily resolution is real and unverified here. The important structural point: the underlying VMS pings ARE individually timestamped, so a monthly product is a processing choice rather than a data limitation. For the dredging half, the klapplads register has 162 active and 88 decommissioned footprints and no date field at all - though comparing across six plan vintages would bracket decommissioning to a plan cycle.

W6.note: HALF ANSWERED, AND THE HALF DEPENDS ON WHICH DEPTH. W6 needs high-frequency records analysed for rates rather than means. The CTD record on disk gives 155,003 casts at 1,502 stations, but the median station has thirteen visits in total; about 150 workhorse stations get twenty to twenty-five a year back to 1976, which is fortnightly for fifty years - ample for extremes and multi-year rates, not enough for the onset rate of an event over days. Genuinely high-frequency water temperature does exist: DMI's oceanObs tw parameter, 31 stations at 10-minute resolution, verified back to at least 2000 - but those are tide gauges, so coastal and near-surface, not at the bed. And no Danish-population thermal experiment using a rate treatment was found; the nearest is a German Baltic Mytilus heat-wave study.

W7.note: The functional half is a desk exercise and the genetic half is a single snapshot. Population-relevant Danish sampling exists in ENA for all three obvious species - 31 Zostera marina samples across two studies, one Danish locality in the 602-sample Skagerrak mussel study, 11 Oresund cod in a 250-sample Swedish study - and every one is a single time point. No genetic time series exists for any Danish marine species, which is what W7's 'through time' requires. Functional diversity through time, by contrast, is computable today from ODA fauna joined to a trait table.

W8.note: No deposited Danish post-hypoxia benthic recolonisation series - five PANGAEA searches and six candidate datasets checked individually - which suggests the classic Kattegat work predates deposit norms. But the local files change what is possible: the station register on disk carries a start and end date for each of 798,574 marine sites, the fauna record is station-resolved with replicates, and the iltsvind bulletins date the events. So whether ODA has fauna stations sampled both before and after a known hypoxia event is answerable from data already held, and nobody has asked.

Z1.note: The floor is very well covered and the ceiling does not exist. Kd, Lysprocent and Secchi give light at the bed against the 11-14 per cent eelgrass requirement, now with 2.37 million rows on disk back to 1988 and a satellite Kd490 field to fill the gaps between stations. No photoinhibition or UV threshold for any Danish species was found, so the upper tail Z1 insists on cannot be placed - which is precisely the asymmetry the hypothesis is about, reproduced in the data.

Z2.note: The proxy exists and the trend cannot be tested. FDOM - an in-situ optical proxy for coloured dissolved organic matter - is in the CTD file at 211 stations, 890,921 rows, and has never been used. It starts in 2021. Z2's claim is that CDOM export has been RISING across Nordic waters, and a five-year sensor record cannot test a trend. The only genuinely spectral Danish coastal dataset is Roskilde Fjord, 230-440 nm, for twenty months in 2014-2015, and searches for sibling datasets by the same authors return their Finnish and Arctic work instead.

Z3.note: The only hypothesis in this pass where no candidate source could be identified even to test. No phenological observation series for Danish marine invertebrates - spawning timing, settlement timing, anything keyed to daylength. Note the connection to W3: the plankton timing IS sampled fortnightly at fifteen stations, so the environmental clock is observed and the organisms' clock is not.

Z4.note: Fifty-three million rows of temperature back to 1970, fortnightly at 150 stations, are on disk - so Z4's extremes-not-means argument is computable now, and no pre-built Danish or Baltic marine-heatwave index exists, which means the Hobday method would have to be run on the reanalysis already held. The rate half is the same constraint as W6: fortnightly resolves multi-year rates and not event onset, and the 10-minute record is at the coast rather than the bed.

Z5.note: The project already computes bed shear from 31 years of hourly wind, which is the field Z5 needs; what is missing is anything to validate it against. No measured near-bed current record for Danish waters was located, and EMODnet Seabed Habitats' energy layer - one of the EUSeaMap inputs - could not be reached to see whether it is separately downloadable. Z5's discriminator is the whole distribution of bed shear against community composition, and the community side is in ODA.

Z6.note: THE BIGGEST SURPRISE IN THIS PASS, AND IT WAS ALREADY BEING COLLECTED. Denmark has run continuous ambient-noise monitoring at eight fixed stations from January 2014 to March 2026, lodged openly in the ICES register by Aarhus University - 345 monthly files, the BIAS grid continued as national monitoring rather than a campaign that ended. Alongside it the impulsive register gives 462 dated, positioned Danish events in 2018 alone, split into pile driving, airguns and 30 explosions. Against the AIS traffic and construction dates this project already holds, the exposure side of Z6 is fully served. THE RESPONSE SIDE IS EMPTY: no Danish settlement or recruitment measurement exists, so 'settlement rates against ambient noise' has one term and not the other.

Z7.note: Z7 says the routes are dated and mapped and therefore this is testable despite being speculative. Half holds. Danish-named cables are visible only inside Germany's digitisation of its own shelf, so Danish coverage is whatever crosses the border; EMODnet has no Danish national cable layer among its 165; the one layer whose schema carries installation year and status returns zero Danish features; and Havplan Danmark serves a JavaScript shell to every path. Energinet's own interconnector commissioning dates were not chased and are the obvious next step. The biological response is not measured at all.

Z8.note: MOVED FROM IMPOSSIBLE TO APPROXIMATE, BY A FILE ALREADY ON DISK. Z8 says Kd is measured and its cause is assumed, and that is confirmed three ways: ODA publishes one broadband number, the operational Copernicus Baltic ocean-colour product carries no absorption partition at all, and PANGAEA holds exactly one Danish spectral dataset. But the CTD extract carries FDOM, Turbiditet and Lysdaempning ON THE SAME CASTS - a coloured-dissolved term, a particle term and a total - which is a first-order partition of the attenuation budget from 2021 onward. It is not a spectral decomposition and it is four years deep, and it is far better than nothing. NOTE THE TURBIDITY GAP: nothing at all between 2008 and 2020, so any attenuation trend spanning it is an instrumentation artefact.

Z9.note: ODA records epiphyte COVER as a percentage per transect point, which is real and is not what Z9's discriminator asks for - it names epiphyte load per unit leaf area against nutrient status and grazer abundance. Neither the biomass nor the grazer count exists for Denmark; the methodological template found is Canadian, from the St Lawrence, which measures sugar, starch and epiphyte load together. The grazers that would crop the epiphytes are in the ODA fauna record, so one of the three terms is closer than it looks.

Z10.note: FOOTPRINTS EVERYWHERE AND DATES ALMOST NOWHERE - except in one register nobody thought to look in. The klapplads WFS gives 162 active and 88 decommissioned dumping grounds with exact polygons and NOT ONE DATE FIELD; the raw-material layer on disk gives 305 licensed areas with an expiry date, no start date and no event record; Femern A/S's legally required turbidity monitoring could not be found at any public endpoint. But the ICES impulsive-noise register carries dated, positioned pile-driving and explosion events, which is a real partial works chronology, and the turbidity to test against is in the CTD file at 252 stations - with the 2008-2020 hole. A crude decommissioning chronology is also derivable by differencing the six klapplads plan vintages.

Z11.note: Z11 needs carbohydrate reserves, tissue sulphide and pathogen load on the same plants, and Denmark has each of the three in a different place or not at all: no rhizome carbohydrate measurement was found anywhere (the nearest analogues are German and Canadian), tissue sulphide exists at three sites in one summer of 2012, and Labyrinthula has been screened at one site in 2011. The shade term is now abundant. It is the plant that is unmeasured - the same conclusion the previous pass reached for K3 and T1, arrived at from a third direction.

gaps.missing: Danish roadside and network ammonia concentration, and the national NH3-from-road-transport emission series. Both are known to exist - EBAS holds the Danish EMEP stations, CEIP WebDab holds the CLRTAP series - and both sit behind interactive interfaces that refused automated access. Also missing: fleet composition by Euro class, which is in no Danmarks Statistik table and is what the stepped-wedge design needs.

Fungicide concentrations in sediment, and fungal biomass. Analyte codes exist for groundwater only; the national status network has 5 sediment stations out of 256 and no coastal station at all; and no ergosterol, chitin or PLFA measurement exists anywhere in Danish marine work.
Avermectin residues in Danish manure, soil, runoff or sediment. VetStat holds the sales at quarterly regional resolution and its per-herd records are access-controlled.

A total biocide load by catchment - and, more basically, the current location of the Danish pesticide sales statistics, which could not be found at any working URL. The mandatory spray journals were not chased.

Marine concentrations of the high-tonnage azoles, strobilurins, SDHIs, neonicotinoids and pyrethroids, and endpoints matched to the conserved target rather than to mortality. The structural cause is now measured: zero coastal stations in the national river-basin-specific-pollutant network.
Any confirmed 6PPD-quinone MEASUREMENT. The analyte code exists nationally, which is more than expected; whether a sample has ever been analysed for it is one query away and was not made.
An ecotoxicological test panel of species actually present in Danish waters. Recorded as a lead rather than a verified absence.
In-situ marine viral abundance at any Danish station. The only Danish viral counts were made in a hydrostatic pressure chamber.
Marine viral community composition. No Danish virome exists in ENA or MGnify, and no Tara Oceans station falls in Danish waters.
Marine fungal biomass, and more than one deployment of fungal community composition. The entire Danish marine fungal barcode record is ten ARMS-MBON ITS rows from one site.
A host condition or disease outcome recorded alongside any of the three Danish eelgrass microbiome datasets. 439 sequencing runs and not one plant health score.
A pre-intervention community baseline for any Danish marine intervention.
A challenge experiment - invasion or infection success in an intact community against a depleted one. The same standard assay as T5's sediment inoculation, not run here.
A defence phenotype measured against microbiome composition.

A national Danish eelgrass or mussel bed polygon layer - EMODnet's pan-European seagrass layer returns zero features for core Danish waters - and a deposited larval connectivity matrix for the Danish straits.
Settlement plates, spat collectors, or any Danish settlement or recruitment measurement whatsoever. This also disables the biological half of Z6.
Trawling effort at monthly or finer resolution. The VMS pings are individually timestamped, so this is a processing choice rather than a data limitation - and every public product is annual.
High-frequency temperature AT THE BED. The 10-minute record is at tide gauges; the bed record is fortnightly. Also missing: any Danish-population thermal tolerance experiment using a rate treatment.
A genetic time series for any Danish marine species. Every population-genomic dataset found is a single snapshot.
A deposited post-hypoxia benthic recolonisation series. But the before-and-after question is answerable from ODA and the local station register, and has not been asked.
A photoinhibition or UV threshold for any Danish species - the ceiling of the light window.
A CDOM record long enough to test a browning TREND. FDOM exists at 211 stations and starts in 2021.
Everything. No phenological observation series for Danish marine invertebrates, and the only hypothesis in this pass for which no candidate source could be identified even to test.
A pre-computed marine heatwave index for Danish waters. The Hobday method on the reanalysis already on disk would produce one.
Measured near-bed currents to validate the modelled bed shear against.
The response side entirely. Twelve years of soundscape at eight stations, and no settlement or recruitment measurement to test it against.
A Danish national submarine cable layer with energisation dates. Danish cables appear only inside Germany's digitisation of its own shelf.

Spectral attenuation partitioned into its components. FDOM plus turbidity plus total gives a first-order partition from 2021; a true decomposition needs a spectroradiometer and exists for one fjord for twenty months.
Epiphyte biomass per unit leaf area, and grazer abundance alongside it. ODA has cover, which is coarser.

Dates. 162 dumping grounds, 88 decommissioned ones and 305 extraction areas, all with exact footprints and no start date or event record; and Femern A/S's legally required turbidity monitoring at no public endpoint.
Eelgrass carbohydrate reserves - no Danish measurement found - and the three variables Z11 needs on the same plants, which exist in three different places or not at all.

_caveats.what_is_different_about_this_pass: The first two passes hunted for sources. This one had 18 GB of data on disk to profile as well, so a large part of it is not 'does this exist' but 'what is actually in the file' - which turned out to be a different question with different answers. Four conclusions in the earlier files change as a result.
_caveats.what_the_lead_verified_personally: The full ODA CTD extract: 53,712,716 rows decompressed and scanned twice, once for the parameter, year, station and QA distribution and once for distinct station-date casts, plus a properly-decoded CSV parse for exact parameter names and units, and a targeted filter recovering the FDOM, Turbiditet, Farvestof and Dihydrogensulfid year histograms. The light and Secchi extracts, row-counted and date-ranged. The station register, 798,574 rows, typed and date-ranged. The CMEMS NetCDF headers, read as raw bytes because no netCDF library is installed. The water-body typology, parsed and its type membership tabulated. The hazardous-substance station layer, parsed and its matrix flags counted. And, because they were load-bearing, three sub-agent findings re-verified from the primary source: the GEUS Jupiter substance catalogue, the ICES continuous-noise submission list and the ICES impulsive-noise register.
_caveats.corrections_to_the_earlier_files: FOUR. (1) K1 no longer needs an authenticated ICES DOME extraction - data_sources_2.json called that the highest-value follow-up in the pass, and a daily 1 km satellite diatom-chlorophyll field for 1997-2016 was already sitting in data/raw/cmems/grid. The DOME extraction is still the better measurement, and it is no longer the only route. (2) The ODA CTD topic carries 17 parameters in the data, not the 12 the portal's criterion pane advertises; the five extra are FDOM, Turbiditet, Stroemhastighed, Stroemretning, Farvestof and Dihydrogensulfid, and FDOM in particular is an unused CDOM proxy that partly answers Z8. (3) The Secchi extract on disk is the two-year default window, not the 1983-2024 record - the date-format bug documented in the last file bit exactly where it was predicted to. (4) F12's premise that Denmark has no invertebrate mortality-response capability is too strong: DTU Aqua is the designated National Reference Laboratory for mollusc diseases.
_caveats.the_shape_of_the_finding: The first pass found Denmark strong on load and weak on disturbance. The second found it strong on geometry and blank on the chemistry of living things. This one finds a third pattern, and it is about ceilings and dates. Every physical field in group Z is measured well at the bottom of its range and not at all at the top - there is a light floor and no photoinhibition threshold, a temperature record and no heatwave index, a modelled bed shear and no measured near-bed current. And every seabed disturbance is published as a footprint with the date removed: 162 dumping grounds and 88 decommissioned ones with no date field at all, 305 extraction areas with an expiry and no start, annual trawling effort over timestamped VMS pings. Denmark publishes where the seabed may be disturbed and not when it was.
_caveats.the_answerable_now_list: From data already on disk or one open query away, with no new collection: K1's diatom share (satellite functional types, daily, 1997-2016, against ODA silicate); Z4's temperature extremes (53.7M rows back to 1970); W3's phenological match-mismatch (fortnightly plankton at 15 stations, confirmed from the programme description, against the daily satellite bloom field); Z6's exposure side (twelve years of soundscape at eight stations plus 462 dated impulsive events in 2018 alone); Z8's first-order attenuation partition from 2021 (FDOM, turbidity and total attenuation on the same casts); W4's density-resolved recruitment (counts per 143 cm2 grab with replicates); W8's before-and-after (station register with per-site start and end dates, fauna station-resolved, iltsvind bulletins dating the events); L5's reference-site arithmetic (14 of 123 water bodies are alone in their WFD type). E20 is one open database away rather than on disk.
_caveats.the_single_most_valuable_follow_up: Re-run the Maaledybde extract with a DD-MM-YYYY period. It recovers a continuous 1983-2024 Secchi record at up to 1,505 stations - the longest optical series Denmark has and the one L3's start-year argument depends on - and the fix is a date-format change in scripts/fetch_oda.py, which still sends ISO.
_caveats.operational_warnings: Three. The ODA date format is DD-MM-YYYY and YYYY-MM-DD silently returns the default window, which is how the Secchi extract came out two years deep. The CTD and light files are iso-8859-1 with semicolon delimiters AND embedded semicolons in free-text fields, so they must be read as quoted CSV - an awk pass produced a nonsense date range before this was noticed. And this VM's /tmp is a 1 GB tmpfs which sub-agents filled to 100% by dumping raw API responses to stdout, which will silently break concurrent work; it had to be truncated mid-pass.
_caveats.what_this_pass_could_not_reach: Danish government sites are increasingly JavaScript applications that serve nothing to a fetch: retsinformation.dk, havplan.dk, VetStat, Danmarks Arealinformation and DTU Aqua's site search all return app shells. EUR-Lex returned an empty body twice. Miljoestyrelsen's site has been reorganised and the pesticide statistics are in neither its sitemap nor its successor's. Two Danish GIS hostnames failed DNS from the sandbox. Where a conclusion depends on one of these, it is marked unverified rather than stated - and one sub-agent inference that did not survive checking, that unit-conversion factors in the Jupiter catalogue imply real measurements, has been removed rather than repeated.
